batchName: Empire: Claudius and Nero (AD 41-68) - Medium Batch 2

questions.question: Whom did Claudius's family hire to discipline him, believing his condition came from laziness?
questions.explanation: A former mule-driver was hired to discipline him. His mother even called him a monster and used him as her yardstick for stupidity.
questions.sourceQuote: A former mule-driver was hired to discipline him, on the theory that his condition came from laziness.

questions.question: Why do modern historians think Claudius married Agrippina?
options: He needed her bloodline's prestige while Britannicus was a child
She had led armies in Germany
He was captivated by her charms
questions.explanation: Ancient writers said she won him with her charms, but modern historians see politics: her bloodline gave prestige while his son was still young. He later made her son Nero joint heir.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern historians see politics: Claudius needed the prestige of her bloodline, and his son Britannicus was still a child.

questions.question: What sparked the rebellion against Nero in March AD 68?
options: Boudica's daughters raised Britain in revolt
A governor in Gaul rebelled against Nero's taxes
A Parthian invasion of the east
The Praetorian Guard proclaimed a new emperor
questions.explanation: The governor of part of Gaul rebelled over taxes and urged the governor of Spain to claim the throne. Even the guard commander later abandoned Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: In March AD 68 the governor of part of Gaul rebelled against Nero's taxes and urged the governor of Spain to claim the throne.

questions.question: How much did Claudius give each guardsman after his accession?
questions.explanation: Each guardsman received 15,000 sesterces. Critics called it the first time an emperor had bought the army's loyalty, though earlier emperors had left similar gifts in their wills.
questions.sourceQuote: He rewarded each guardsman with 15,000 sesterces.

questions.question: What did Tacitus admit about histories of these emperors?
options: They were copied from Claudius's books
They were falsified from fear, then written in fresh hatred
They were all written by freedmen
They were lost in the Great Fire
questions.explanation: Tacitus admitted histories were falsified out of fear while the emperors lived and written in fresh hatred after they died. A Jewish historian likewise complained of flattery and lies about Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: Tacitus himself admitted that histories of these emperors were falsified out of fear while they lived and written in fresh hatred after they died.

questions.question: Which measures did Claudius take to end Rome's winter grain shortages? (select all that apply)
options: Built a new harbour north of Ostia
Insured merchants sailing to Egypt in winter
Added a lighthouse to the new harbour
questions.explanation: Claudius built a new harbour with a lighthouse north of Ostia and insured merchants who risked winter voyages to Egypt. He also brought two new aqueducts into Rome in AD 52.
questions.sourceQuote: To end winter grain shortages, he built a new harbour north of Ostia, Rome's port, with a lighthouse, and insured merchants who risked winter voyages to Egypt.

questions.question: Why were the senators forced to accept Claudius as emperor in AD 41?
options: They voted unanimously for him at once
The people rioted until the Senate gave way
He was the named heir in his nephew's will
His legions marched on the Senate house
They argued over who should rule, and he refused to appear
questions.explanation: The Senate fell to arguing over which senator should rule, then demanded Claudius appear for approval. He wisely refused, and they had to accept him.
questions.sourceQuote: Meanwhile the Senate (*senatus*), Rome's council of elder statesmen, debated a change of government but fell to arguing over which of its members should rule.

questions.question: How did Nero pay for rebuilding Rome after the fire?
options: Raising taxes and debasing the coinage
questions.explanation: Nero raised taxes and debased the coinage. The new city had brick houses on wider streets.
questions.sourceQuote: To pay for it, Nero raised taxes and debased the coinage.

questions.question: What made Britain a tempting target for Roman conquest? (select all that apply)
options: It had sheltered rebels from Gaul
questions.explanation: Britain offered mines and potential slaves and had sheltered rebels from Gaul. The immediate trigger was an appeal from a British ally driven from his lands.
questions.sourceQuote: The island tempted Rome with its mines and potential slaves, and it had sheltered rebels from Gaul.

questions.question: What did Claudius use the revived office of censor to do?
options: Expel all freedmen from public office
Admit nobles from Gaul into the Senate
questions.explanation: As censor he admitted Gallic nobles to the Senate, and his speech survives on a bronze plaque found at Lyon. The censor kept the lists of citizens and senators.
questions.sourceQuote: He used it to admit nobles from Gaul into the Senate, a speech still preserved on a bronze plaque found at Lyon.
